need.current_gap: The current control artifact uses fixed layer, direction, and dose; expanding the action schema is unjustified until an oracle-per-instance arm shows headroom and a deployable bounded ranker recovers it on held-out inputs.
falsification_criteria: The oracle schedule has no meaningful lift over the fixed executor, so the action schema remains fixed.
Oracle headroom exists but no bounded ranker recovers it, so the result remains research-only.
Any lift disappears against random-layer, sensor-off, dose, latency, or capability-tax controls.
protected_boundaries: This Demand cannot run until substrate control authority has a named-human PROCEED outcome and a separate runnable task is designed.
The scheduler may act only in bounded controller z_t space; no base-model or token-space RL update is authorized.
Evaluation and human judgments remain read-only validation anchors and never become learning reward.
need.required_outcome: Compare fixed executor, matched ReFT challenger, per-instance oracle subset, prompt-only ranker, random layer subset, and sensor-off unconditional controls under equal norm, compute, and evaluation budgets.
success_criteria: The oracle per-instance schedule has preregistered lift over the best fixed schedule on target effect and damage-adjusted utility.
A bounded ranker recovers the required fraction of oracle lift on held-out inputs while reducing reverse effects or already-correct damage.
Checkpoint round-trip preserves exact schedule decisions and artifact lineage.

objective: Determine whether a per-instance layer/dose scheduler has material held-out headroom over a fixed global residual executor and whether a bounded ranker can recover that oracle headroom without increasing reverse effects or capability damage.
title: Measure per-instance layer and dose scheduling headroom
